advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls `run_detached(store, "")` and asserts it degrades to default tunables / stamps without crashing, pinning the empty-string→None coercion in run_detached.
evidence: gc_trigger.py:211-213: `# ... the detached stub hands "" through for an absent repo root, so coerce it back to None here` / `repo_root = repo_root or None`
commit message: "The old stub's `sys.argv[2] or None` coercion moves into run_detached itself (`repo_root = repo_root or None`) -- identical semantics for every caller."
test_spawn_detached.py:145,154: the spawner is verified to place `""` on argv (`captured.argv[4] == ""`), i.e. the child WILL receive `""` as repo_root

search of tests/unit for `run_detached(str(store), "")` returns (no matches); existing run_detached tests pass `str(repo)` (test_snapshot_gc_trigger.py:282,301,325) or `str(gone)` (line 344), never the empty-string sentinel

ABSENCE: with no test exercising the `""` input, a regression that drops the coercion (letting `""` reach `_janitor.JanitorConfig.from_env("")` at gc_trigger.py:167) would not be caught by any test in the suite
advisory.finding: The empty-string sentinel → None coercion newly relocated into run_detached (`repo_root = repo_root or None`) is untested: no test drives `run_detached(store, "")`, which is exactly the argv value the shared spawner now hands the detached child. Every existing run_detached test passes a real path string or None, so removing/breaking the coercion would go undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor removes or alters `repo_root = repo_root or None`, causing the detached child to pass an empty string to JanitorConfig.from_env instead of degrading to defaults
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_run_detached_coerces_empty_repo_root_sentinel_to_none` that invokes `gc_trigger.run_detached(str(store), "")` and asserts the pass runs against default JanitorConfig (e.g. monkeypatch `_janitor_config`/`from_env` to record the coerced argument is None), mirroring the dead-repo-root test at line 339.
